title: Hardcourt Divide — Championship Broadcast Slate
description: A diagonal split-field promo built for high-stakes sports matchups: two team identities at equal weight flank an oversized VS mark, jersey-number outlines ghost the background, and a monospaced scoreboard strip locks in tipoff details with broadcast precision.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment before the whistle blows — the pre-game card, the arena lobby screen, the social post that makes a routine matchup feel like a must-watch event. It borrows the visual grammar of live broadcast motion graphics: hard diagonals, massive numerals, and typographic mass that reads from an LED board at fifty feet. It flatly refuses decorative softness, gradient ambiguity, or anything that whispers when it should shout. Every element is intentional, loud, and unapologetic — built for audiences who feel the energy before they read a single word of copy.
goodFor: Basketball and football game-day announcement slides
Social media countdown cards pitting two rival teams or brands
Esports tournament matchup promo screens and bracket reveals
Sports venue lobby or jumbotron pre-game event previews
avoidFor: Multi-team bracket formats requiring more than two opponents on one slide
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews needing data legibility
Layouts requiring dense body copy or fine-print footnotes
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the moment arena lights drop — two rival forces locked in hard confrontation across a diagonal fault line, neither yielding an inch. Visual energy radiates from the VS mark outward, with phantom jersey numerals looming behind each half like crowd noise made visible. The mood is live broadcast pre-game card: confrontational, electric, and unapologetically loud. Avoid softness, decorative curves, gradient ambiguity, or any compositional element that suggests harmony over rivalry.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas split by a hard diagonal running upper-left to lower-right, dividing the field into two equal team identity zones with no gutter between them. Each half anchors its team name flush to the outer edge with maximum typographic mass, while ghost jersey-number outlines bleed behind as watermark-scale texture filling the entire zone. The VS lockup straddles the diagonal centerline as the singular undisputed focal point of the composition. A full-width monospaced scoreboard strip runs edge-to-edge at the bottom with zero outer margin, locking in game date, tipoff time, and venue at broadcast-legibility scale.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a frozen broadcast frame — kinetic tension compressed into a still image, two rival identities carved apart by an uncompromising diagonal fault line. Each half radiates equal authority, its stat callouts monumental and confrontational, while ghosted jersey numerals hum behind like crowd noise rendered typographic. Dense mass anchors both outer extremes; the composition breathes only at the central seam where the VS mark holds the cut. Avoid softness, rounded elements, or decorative borders — every edge should feel like it was ruled with a steel straight edge, not drawn.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-col grid split by a hard diagonal blade running from lower-left to upper-right, dividing the field into two mirrored team zones — each zone owns cols 1-5 and 8-12 respectively, with two to three stat callouts per side anchored to the outer columns (oversized numeral stacked above a compact label line). Jersey-number outlines ghost at large scale behind each zone's content, bled to the outer corners and sitting below the active layer. The central VS lockup straddles the diagonal seam at vertical midpoint, overlapping both halves and acting as the visual spine. A full-bleed monospaced scoreboard strip locks flush to the bottom edge, carrying venue, tip-off time, and broadcast channel in a single dense row with no bottom margin.
